version.changelog: Remove SumatraPDF/soffice from requires.bins; scripts locate them via path search

llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate local printing and document utility, but it gives an agent broad document-editing and direct-printing authority without a confirmation-first safety model.

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently describe printing plus PDF, Office, and photo workflows, but the capability set is broad: Office content edits, slide deletion, PDF encryption/decryption, watermarking, merging, splitting, and direct print dispatch are all bundled into one print-assistant skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: CLAUDE.md explicitly says printing happens directly without confirmation once an instruction is understood, while natural-language routing covers file mutation and PDF decryption. Preview is recommended only for layout-heavy requests, not as a default safety gate.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The install path is disclosed: pip installs requirements, and setup.ps1 installs SumatraPDF and LibreOffice with winget, then creates printer config. This is purpose-related, but users should review the PowerShell setup and dependencies before running them.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Windows-only access to local printers, LibreOffice conversion, SumatraPDF printing, and optional Adobe MCP authentication fit the stated workflows. No hidden network exfiltration, credential-store access, or background worker behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The tools persist transformed Office/PDF/image outputs and can write an unencrypted PDF copy after decryption. They also create local printer configuration. No covert persistence was found, but write operations lack built-in confirmation, overwrite prevention, or cleanup guarantees.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent that can print immediately, modify Office files, transform PDFs, and create decrypted PDF copies. Review setup.ps1 first, configure printers carefully, prefer preview or explicit confirmation before print jobs, and avoid using it on confidential documents unless you control the printer and output locations.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell-based setup is disclosed and purpose-related; I did not find hidden installer behavior, but the PowerShell and package installation steps still warrant user review.
[TP4] expected: The broad document-manipulation features are disclosed in SKILL.md, README.md, and CLAUDE.md, so this is not deceptive tool poisoning; it remains relevant because the bundled authority is broad for a print assistant.
[SDI-1] expected: Office editing is explicitly documented, including natural-language routing. The concern is not hidden capability, but lack of a separate consent boundary for document mutation.
[SDI-2] expected: General DOCX/XLSX/PPTX write functions are real and disclosed. They save to caller-provided output paths, so they are user-directed but still high-impact if an agent routes casually worded requests into edits.
[SDI-2] expected: PDF decryption is advertised and requires a password, but it writes a plaintext output file, which users should treat as sensitive persistent data.
[SQP-2] expected: Direct printing without confirmation is explicitly instructed and central to the skill, but it is an irreversible real-world action with possible privacy and resource impact.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad natural-language examples are expected for this assistant style, but they increase accidental activation risk when combined with direct printing and write-capable document tools.
[SQP-2] expected: Office save behavior is normal for the documented edit functions; the missing safety layer is user confirmation or a clear default to non-destructive copies.
